Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
-----
For the Petitioner : Mr. Baban Prasad, Advocate For the State : Mr. Praful Jojo, Addl.P.P.

For the Informant : Mr. Abhay Kr. Chaturvedy, Advocate -------
Order No.02/ Dated: 21.03.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending their arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 1299 of 2022 instituted under Section 323, 341 and 498A of IPC, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
It has been alleged that complainant was married with the petitioner on 09.05.2022 as per Hindu Rites and Rituals.

Mother and brother of the complainant gifted cash of Rs.3,83,000 and freeze,
cooler, washing machine, mixy, godrez almirah, dressing table, bed, trunk, utensils of steel and bronze, Pulser bike, gold chain and ring at the time of vidai and after one day accused persons started taunting for bring substandard articles and started torturing her and started demanding car and branded articles.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is lastly submitted that the petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the investigation of the case and also abide by all terms and conditions which may be imposed in the matter of granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.

sentences.text: Considering the factual aspect of the matter, it is an official complaint case and there is no necessity of custodial trial of the petitioner.
Hence, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, this anticipatory bail application is disposed off.

Petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court below within a period of four weeks and seek regular bail which shall be disposed off on its own merits in compliance of the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr., reported in 2021(10) SCC 773.
